label: bastar-dhokra/process/core-to-mould
title: From the core to the mould
description: Three steps of a Bastar dhokra mould: the core rubbed green with sem leaves, wound in wax strings and coated in soil.

u0001.text: The core is coated green, wound in wax and closed in soil before it is fired.

u0004.text: Wax strings are wrapped closely around the hard, green-coated model.

u0007.text: The waxed model is coated with sieved riverside soil and powdered wood coal.

C055.text: Crushed leaves of the sem or country bean creeper are rubbed over the dry model until it turns green, to keep the next soil from sticking to it.

quotes.quote: Fresh and 'semi' or 'sem' or country bean creeper leaves are brought, crushed by rubbing them between both palms till a green liquid oozes out.
all over the model until the models looks totally green. This is to prevent the soil from sticking to the model
The purpose of applying green liquid to model is to prevent the soil from sticking to the model.

C061.text: Wax strings are wrapped closely around the hard, green-coated model, and further designs are added in plain wax.

quotes.quote: When wax strings are ready as required, they are wrapped closely around the model, which is hard and dry and green with the application of sem-leaf liquid. When the model is totally covered with wax strings, designs of choice can be made with plain wax too.
7. Wrapping of strings (Tikkal Chadana): Wax strings are tightly wrapped around the dry clay form

C064.text: The waxed model is first coated with sieved riverside soil and powdered wood coal, mixed in proportions of about 85-90% soil to 10-15% coal.

quotes.quote: Powdered sticky riverside soil and powdered wood coal are sieved separately through clean cloth. Mixed in the proportions 90-85% and 10-15%, water is added and kneaded to make dough like consistency and applied over the model.
